highlight.text: The portrait features life-sized depictions of Charles IV of Spain and his family, ostentatiously dressed in fine costume and jewellery.

source.author: Wikipedia contributors
source.title: Charles IV of Spain and His Family

work.text: He began work on the painting in 1800, shortly after he became First Chamber Painter to the royal family, and completed it in the summer of 1801.

source.author: Wikipedia contributors
source.title: Charles IV of Spain and His Family

moment.text: The painting was modelled after Louis-Michel van Loo's 1743 Portrait of Felipe V and his Family and Velázquez's Las Meninas, setting the royal subjects in a similarly naturalistic setting as they pose for the artist who is visible at his easel at the left of the canvas.

source.author: Wikipedia contributors
source.title: Charles IV of Spain and His Family

matters.text: Although a formal portrait, there are indications of intimacy between the family members; Queen Maria Luisa holds the hand of the youngest child.
